newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-ITALY CONTENT WITH GOALLESS DRAW VS POLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY CONTENT WITH GOALLESS DRAW VS POLAND.

text.p: Italy lost their 100 per cent record in European qualifying group two when they were held to a 0-0 draw by Poland on Wednesday.
Apart from a few isolated chances the Italians played cautiously and defensively throughout and although Poland made more chances they rarely looked like scoring.

Despite dropping their first two points of the campaign Italy remain top of the group with 13 points from five matches, England are second with nine from four and Poland third with four from three. Neither Georgia or Moldova have any points.
The best chance of the night came in the 44th minute when Pawel Wojtala headed over from close range after goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi mishandled a free-kick.

"We had a chance to win as Italy created no real scoring situations and we had one. We wanted three points and we got one point but our chances of qualifying are not over" Polish coach Antoni Piechniczek said.
Italy appeared to content to play for a draw with their strikers laregly isolated from the midfield who gave them little creative support.

Italy's best chances came from set plays when Giafranco Zola's free kick from 30 metres wenmt narrowly wide in the 23rd minute and Christian Vieri's header from a corner kick was punched clear by Polish keeper Andrzej Wozniak in the 41st minute.
"I am very pleased with the match. My team arrived very tired but did its job," Italian coach Cesare Maldini said.
The Italians beat Moldova 3-0 on Saturday although Maldini's tactics seemed pre-ordained rather than the Italians showing real signs of tiredness.
Danish referee Kim Nielsen booked Italy's Vieri, Dino Baggio, Alessandro Costacurta and Roberto Di Matteo and Poland's Adam Ledwon.
